induction chemotherapy (ICT)/CCRT and CCRRT had similar overall survival (OS) in patients with locally advanced PLSCC, but poorer progression-free survival (PFs) and locoregion control (LRC), were seen in the ICT/CRRT arm.
induction chemotherapy followed by concurrent chemo-radiation therapy did not improve the overall survival of patients with advanced pharnyngolaryngeal cancer.
induction chemotherapy (ICT)/CCRT was inferior to CCRT alone in terms of progression-free survival (p = 0015) and locoregiona control (p = 0026), but not overall survival (p =.045).

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the addition of neoadjuvant therapy did not improve the survival of patients with advanced PLSCC, but the compliance to CCRT was inferior in the neoadjuvant group.
ICT followed by CCRT is associated with inferior PFS and LCR compared to CCRT alone in patients with advanced-stage pharyngeal or laryngeal cancer, although OS was similar between the 2 arms.
the addition of ICT to CCRT did not improve OS but decreased LRC and PPS in patients with advanced PLSCC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
induction chemotherapy is not superior to concurrent chemoradiotherapies for patients with advanced squamous cell carcinomas of the pharyngeal or laryngeal region.
induction chemotherapy followed by concurrent radiochemotherapy is inferior to concurrent radiochemotherapy alone for patients with advanced squamous cell carcinomas of the pharyngolaryngeal region.
the addition of ICT did not improve OS in patients with advanced PLSCC, and the inferior compliance to CCRT in the ICT arm may be a major factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the sequential approach of neoadjuvant therapy and CCRT does not improve the survival of patients with advanced-stage pharyngeal or laryngeal cancer, but the compliance of CCRT was poorer in the sequential approach.

the addition of induction chemotherapy (IC) did not improve the overall survival of patients with advanced squamous cell cancer of the pharyngeal or laryngeal region, compared with concurrent chemoradiation therapy (CCRT) alone.
induction chemotherapy followed by concurrent radiochemotherapy did not improve the outcome of advanced larynx and hypopharyngeal cancer.
